name: Information / data visualization
controls: Which information graphics appear in the piece (numbers, charts, maps, diagrams, tables) and how their data is animated into view and through change.
question: Does the piece need to show numbers, charts or diagrams, and which kinds?
notes: In motion, a chart is a sequence, not a picture: axes and context first, then the data, then the highlight, then the takeaway; the 'technique' facet names the animation verbs. Keep one idea per chart and one highlighted datum per beat. Animate from a meaningful baseline (zero for bars, the previous value for updates) and never animate in a way that misrepresents magnitude (no bars growing past their value with overshoot unless the value is labelled first, no truncated axes hidden by motion). Counters and statistics are the most-used data device in product films; real charts are more common in explainers, finance and analytics products. Build in HTML/SVG: bars as divs or rects scaling from their baseline, lines as SVG paths drawn with stroke-dashoffset, donuts as circles with stroke-dasharray, numbers counted on a proxy object with snapping (these value tweens are exempt from motion-language checks). 'Sankey-style' and 'knowledge graph' are used loosely in marketing; a strict Sankey has flow widths proportional to quantity. Combinations are common: a statistic plus a progress ring, a map plus counters, a dashboard assembled from bars, lines and status indicators.

options.what: A numeral that animates from a start value to its final value, by counting or by rolling digits.
options.looks: Large tabular numerals ticking up, or odometer-style digit columns rolling into place.
options.motion: Count-up on a proxy object with snapped integers over 800-1600ms, decelerating (power2.out to expo.out) so the last digits settle slowly.
options.use: Launch films (users, speed, savings), stats slides, results, social proof.
options.vs: A statistic is the whole composed fact (number, unit, label, context); a counter is only the animated numeral technique.
options.prompt: Count the number from 0 (or from a meaningful previous value) to its final value by tweening a proxy object and writing Math.round(value) with thousands separators into a tabular-nums element over 1000-1600ms with expo.out; for an odometer look, roll each digit column on yPercent with 40ms stagger from the right.

options.what: A composed data fact: a hero number with its unit, label and context line, presented as a typographic moment.
options.looks: Oversized numeral (160-400px), smaller unit and label, a one-line source or comparison, lots of negative space.
options.motion: Number counts up or reveals via mask, label and context arrive after, optional accent underline or delta badge.
options.use: Product films, investor updates, impact reports, social stat posts.
options.conveys: Credibility, confidence, a single memorable proof point.
options.vs: Comparison cards set two or more statistics against each other; a statistic stands alone.
options.prompt: Compose the statistic typographically: hero number at 200-360px in the display face with tabular numerals, unit at 40% size aligned to the cap height, label below at 28-36px; reveal the number with a count-up or mask rise first, then the label 200ms later, then the context line; hold 1.5s or more.

options.what: Categorical values encoded as bar lengths from a common baseline.
options.looks: Vertical columns or horizontal bars, minimal axes, value labels at bar ends, one highlighted bar.
options.motion: Bars grow from the baseline with a stagger in reading order; labels count up with them; the highlighted bar recolors after.
options.use: Comparisons, benchmarks, growth over periods, survey results.
options.vs: Ranking lists sort items by value with labels as the focus; bar charts emphasize magnitudes. Comparison cards show two values as typography.
options.prompt: Draw the axis baseline first (scaleX 0 to 1), then grow each bar with scaleY 0 to 1 from transform-origin bottom, staggered 80-120ms left to right, with its value label counting in sync; finally recolor the key bar to the accent and dim the others to 40%. No overshoot past the true value.

options.what: Values over a continuous dimension (usually time) connected as a line.
options.looks: A single confident line on light gridlines, an endpoint dot with value label, annotations at key events.
options.motion: The line draws left to right via stroke-dashoffset, a leading dot rides the tip, annotations pop as the line passes them.
options.use: Growth stories, performance over time, trends, before/after inflection points.
options.vs: Area charts fill beneath the line to emphasize volume; line graphs emphasize trend and exact shape.
options.prompt: Draw the line as an SVG path with stroke-dasharray equal to its length and tween stroke-dashoffset to 0 over 1200-2000ms with power2.inOut, while a 10px dot follows the tip (MotionPath or getPointAtLength); show gridlines first at 10-15% contrast; fire annotation labels as the tip passes their x.

options.what: A line chart with the region below the line filled, emphasizing cumulative volume.
options.looks: Filled gradient regions under a line, stacked layers for composition.
options.motion: Fill rises from the baseline or wipes left to right with the line; stacked layers build one at a time.
options.use: Usage growth, revenue composition, traffic volume.
options.vs: Line graphs show trend precisely; area charts show magnitude and part-to-whole when stacked.
options.prompt: Reveal the area with a clip-path inset wipe left to right synchronized with the top line's stroke draw over 1200-1800ms; fill with a vertical gradient from the series color at 60% to 0%; build stacked series one by one, bottom first, with 300ms offsets.

options.what: Part-to-whole proportions as angular segments of a circle (donut: with a hollow center holding a label).
options.looks: Two to five segments, one accented, center label with the key percentage.
options.motion: Segments sweep around the circle in sequence; center number counts up; the key segment pulls out slightly.
options.use: Market share, composition, survey splits.
options.vs: Progress rings show one value toward 100%; donuts show several parts of one whole.
options.prompt: Build each segment as an SVG circle with stroke-dasharray (segment length, circumference) and a rotation offset; sweep segments in sequence with stroke-dashoffset tweens (300-500ms each, 80ms overlap) starting at 12 o'clock clockwise; count the center label; pull the accent segment 8-12px outward along its bisector.

options.what: Individual data points positioned on two axes to show distribution and correlation.
options.looks: Many small dots, a highlighted cluster or outlier, optional trend line.
options.motion: Dots appear with a fast random or axis-ordered stagger, then a cluster highlights and a trend line draws.
options.use: Research, AI and data products, positioning maps (us vs competitors).
options.vs: Heat maps aggregate density into color; scatter plots keep every individual point.
options.prompt: Draw axes, then place 50-400 dots (6-8px) with scale from 0.6 to 1 and stagger {each: 0.01, from: 'random'} (seeded); dim all dots to 30% and highlight the key cluster in the accent; draw a trend line via stroke-dashoffset last.

options.what: A circular stroke that fills to show one value's progress toward a whole.
options.looks: Thick rounded stroke on a faint track, percentage or icon in the center.
options.motion: Stroke sweeps from 12 o'clock with stroke-dashoffset, number counts in sync, a completion accent at 100%.
options.use: Goals, completion, scores, health and fitness metrics, uptime.
options.vs: Progress bars are linear and read as process; rings read as score or goal. Donuts divide a whole into several parts.
options.prompt: Draw a track circle at 10-15% opacity and a progress circle with stroke-linecap round, rotated -90deg; tween stroke-dashoffset from circumference to circumference times (1 - value) over 1000-1400ms with power2.out while the center number counts in sync.

options.what: A linear bar that fills to show progress through a process or toward a value.
options.looks: Rounded track and fill, optional percentage label riding the fill edge, step markers.
options.motion: Fill scales on x from the left in uneven chunks, label follows the edge.
options.use: Uploads, onboarding, deploys, goals, comparisons of completion.
options.vs: Progress rings suit scores; progress bars suit processes and sequences.
options.prompt: Fill the bar with scaleX from transform-origin left in 2-4 uneven chunks (e.g. 0 to 0.35, pause 200ms, to 0.8, to 1) using the motion language's move ease; keep the label pinned to the fill edge and switch the fill color or add a check when complete.

options.what: Geographic data: regions, routes, locations or expansion shown on a map.
options.looks: Simplified vector map, highlighted regions, pins, arcs connecting cities, minimal labels.
options.motion: Camera zooms from global to local, regions fill, pins drop, route arcs draw between locations.
options.use: Global reach, expansion, logistics, travel, network coverage.
options.vs: Heat maps can be geographic but encode intensity by color; a map focuses on places and connections.
options.prompt: Use a simplified SVG map at low contrast (landmass at 8-15% ink); zoom the camera from global to region over 1200-1600ms; fill highlighted regions with the accent (opacity or clip wipe), drop pins with a short scale settle, and draw curved arcs between cities with stroke-dashoffset, staggered 150ms.

options.what: A grid or area where value intensity is encoded as color.
options.looks: Cells in a sequential color ramp (e.g. GitHub-style contribution grid), a legend, a highlighted hotspot.
options.motion: Cells fill with a diagonal or time-ordered cascade, intensity rises, a hotspot pulses.
options.use: Activity, usage patterns, risk, performance, contribution graphs.
options.vs: Scatter keeps individual points; heat maps aggregate into cells.
options.prompt: Lay out a cell grid (e.g. 52x7 or 24x7) with 2-4px gaps; fill cells from the empty color to their ramp color with stagger {each: 0.004, grid: 'auto', from: 'start'} over 1200-2000ms total; then outline or pulse the hottest region.

options.what: Events ordered along a time axis.
options.looks: A horizontal or vertical line with dated markers, milestones labelled, current point highlighted.
options.motion: The axis draws on, the camera tracks along it, milestones pop as the playhead reaches them.
options.use: Company history, roadmaps, release histories, process over time.
options.conveys: Progress over time, heritage, momentum toward the future.
options.vs: Process diagrams show logical steps; timelines show chronological position with real dates.
options.prompt: Draw the time axis with scaleX from the left; track the camera along it (world x tween, power2.inOut) while each milestone dot scales in and its date and label reveal from a mask as the playhead passes; highlight 'now' with the accent and a subtle pulse.

options.what: Structured values in rows and columns.
options.looks: Clean rows with hairline separators, tabular numerals, one highlighted row or column.
options.motion: Rows cascade in, a highlight band sweeps to the key row, cells update with rolling numbers, rows re-sort.
options.use: Feature comparisons, pricing, data products, spreadsheet and database tools.
options.vs: Ranking lists are single-column ordered tables focused on position; comparison cards are two or three items, not rows.
options.prompt: Reveal the header row, then cascade rows with a mask rise staggered 50-70ms; use tabular-nums and right-aligned numbers; highlight the key row with a background band that slides to it (y tween) and update changing cells with a vertical digit roll.

options.what: A composed panel of multiple metrics, charts and statuses representing a product's analytics view.
options.looks: Grid or bento of KPI tiles, sparklines, a main chart, status indicators; brand UI styling.
options.motion: Tiles assemble in a cascade, then each chart animates its data in sequence, then one metric is zoomed into.
options.use: Analytics, fintech, monitoring and SaaS product films.
options.vs: UI treatment 'dashboard UI' is about rendering the interface; this option is about animating the data inside it.
options.prompt: Assemble the dashboard in three passes: tile frames cascade in (grid stagger from top-left, 60ms), then each tile's data animates (counters, bar grows, line draws) in reading order, then the camera pushes into the key tile and its metric updates with a delta badge.

options.what: Entities as nodes connected by edges, showing structure or connectivity.
options.looks: Circles or icons linked by thin lines, a central hub, pulses travelling along edges.
options.motion: Nodes appear from the hub outward, edges draw between them, data packets pulse along edges.
options.use: Integrations, infrastructure, networks, social graphs, distributed systems.
options.conveys: Connectivity, ecosystem, scale of a system.
options.vs: Knowledge graphs attach labelled semantic relationships; node networks show connectivity without meaning on each edge. Flow diagrams add direction and sequence.
options.prompt: Place a hub node, then spawn outer nodes with a short scale settle staggered outward by distance; draw 1-1.5px edges with stroke-dashoffset as each node appears; send 4-6px packets along edges (MotionPath) on loops to show live traffic.

options.what: A network of concepts or entities connected by labelled relationships.
options.looks: Labelled nodes (people, documents, concepts) and edges with relation labels, clusters by type or color.
options.motion: A query highlights a path through the graph; neighbors fade in as the focus node expands.
options.use: AI and search products, knowledge tools, data platforms, research.
options.vs: A node network shows connectivity; a knowledge graph shows meaning (each edge is a typed relation).
options.prompt: Show a focus node with its label, then expand first-degree neighbors along labelled edges (edge draws, then relation label reveals), color-coded by entity type; highlight a query path by brightening its edges in sequence and dimming the rest to 20%.

options.what: Steps and decisions connected by directed arrows showing how something proceeds.
options.looks: Boxes and decision diamonds with arrows, a highlighted active path.
options.motion: Arrows draw in direction of flow, a token travels through the path, active steps light up.
options.use: Workflows, automation, logic, onboarding explanations.
options.conveys: Logic, clarity, how the system decides.
options.vs: Process diagrams show linear stages without branching; flow diagrams include decisions and branches.
options.prompt: Reveal nodes in flow order and draw each connecting arrow with stroke-dashoffset in its direction of flow (arrowhead appears at the end); then send a token dot along the active path, lighting each node with the accent on arrival, and take one branch at each decision.

options.what: Flows between stages drawn as bands whose widths are proportional to quantity.
options.looks: Thick curved ribbons splitting and merging between columns of nodes.
options.motion: Ribbons extend from source to target in sequence; widths reveal quantities; one flow highlights.
options.use: Budgets, conversions, energy and material flows, user journeys.
options.conveys: Where volume goes; proportion in motion.
options.vs: Funnels show one path narrowing; Sankeys show branching and merging flows. 'Sankey-style' in marketing is often decorative without proportional widths.
options.prompt: Draw ribbons as SVG paths with thickness proportional to value; reveal each ribbon from source to target with a clip-path or mask wipe left to right, stage by stage (400-600ms each); then dim all but one flow to 25% and label its value.

options.what: A linear or cyclical sequence of stages showing how inputs become outputs.
options.looks: Numbered steps in a row or loop with connectors, icons for each stage.
options.motion: Stages activate one after another along a connector; cyclical processes loop.
options.use: How-it-works sections, explainers, onboarding, pipelines.
options.vs: Flow diagrams branch; process diagrams run in one sequence. Timelines use real dates.
options.prompt: Lay out 3-5 stages with a connector line; progress a fill along the connector (scaleX) and activate each stage as the fill reaches it (icon draws on, label reveals, stage accent); for cycles, loop the progress around a circle path.

options.what: Stages that narrow to show drop-off or conversion from one stage to the next.
options.looks: Stacked bars or trapezoids decreasing in width, percentages between stages.
options.motion: Stages appear top to bottom, widths shrink to value, conversion rates count up; an improved funnel widens in a second state.
options.use: Sales and marketing products, conversion stories, before/after optimization.
options.conveys: Efficiency, where value is lost, improvement.
options.vs: Sankeys show branching flows; funnels show one path narrowing.
options.prompt: Build the funnel top down: each stage bar grows from center (scaleX 0 to value) staggered 150ms with its count; label the drop-off between stages; for the payoff, tween stage widths to the improved values and show the delta.

options.what: Two or three cards or columns setting values or features side by side.
options.looks: Symmetric cards, 'before/after' or 'us/them', the winning card accented.
options.motion: Both cards enter together, values count simultaneously, the winner scales up slightly or recolors while the other dims.
options.use: Competitive positioning, before/after, plan comparisons, benchmarks.
options.vs: Statistic callouts stand alone; tables compare many rows; comparison cards compare a few items head to head.
options.prompt: Enter two cards symmetrically (mirrored directions), count their values simultaneously so the difference emerges in time, then dim the losing card to 40% and scale the winner 1 to 1.04 with an accent border; keep typography identical so only values differ.

options.what: Items ordered by value, where position changes are the story.
options.looks: Numbered rows with labels and value bars, the subject row highlighted.
options.motion: Rows reorder with smooth position swaps as values change; the subject climbs to first.
options.use: Leaderboards, benchmark results, 'number one in' claims, bar chart races.
options.vs: Bar charts show static magnitudes; ranking lists animate order.
options.prompt: Render rows absolutely positioned by rank; when values change, tween each row's y to its new rank slot (FLIP) over 400-600ms while value bars rescale and numbers roll; keep the subject row in the accent color and end with it at rank 1.

options.what: Small signals (dots, pills, badges) showing state such as live, healthy, failing or pending.
options.looks: Colored dots with labels, 'Operational' pills, live pulses, check and warning badges.
options.motion: Live pulses (expanding ring loops), color transitions on state change, label rolls.
options.use: Monitoring, DevOps, security, status pages, deploy flows, agent activity.
options.vs: Progress indicators measure advancement; status indicators show discrete state.
options.prompt: Use 8-10px dots with a looping pulse ring (scale 1 to 2.5 with the ring's opacity falling to 0, 1600ms, repeat); on state change recolor the dot over 200ms and roll the label vertically; cascade a column of indicators turning green one by one for 'all systems operational'.

options.what: Marks extend from a baseline to their value (bars, areas, radial segments).
options.prompt: Grow marks from their baseline with scaleY or scaleX 0 to 1 from the baseline origin, staggered in reading order, never overshooting the true value.

options.what: Lines and outlines are drawn progressively along their path.
options.prompt: Draw paths with stroke-dasharray equal to path length and tween stroke-dashoffset to 0, optionally with a leading dot riding the tip.

options.what: Numbers animate from a start value to the final value.
options.prompt: Tween a proxy object's value and write the rounded, formatted result into a tabular-numeral element each update, decelerating into the final digits.

options.what: One datum is made prominent while others recede.
options.prompt: Recolor the key datum to the accent and dim all other marks to 25-40% opacity; add a label or annotation for the highlighted datum only.

options.what: Irrelevant data is removed or dimmed to focus on a subset.
options.prompt: Animate out or dim non-matching marks (opacity to 0.15, scale to 0.9) while matching marks stay, then optionally rescale the axis to the filtered range.

options.what: Items reorder by value to reveal ranking.
options.prompt: Tween each item's position to its sorted slot (FLIP) over 400-600ms with a slight stagger so the reordering is followable.

options.what: The same data points move into a new layout or chart type (e.g. dots becoming bars).
options.prompt: Keep each datum as one persistent element and tween it from its position in layout A to its position in layout B (grid to bar stack, scatter to histogram) so identity is preserved.

options.what: The camera or scale moves into a region of the data to show detail.
options.prompt: Scale the chart container toward the region of interest (transform-origin at the region) while axis labels update to the new range; fade in finer detail at the zoomed level.

options.what: Information is revealed in layers: context, then data, then insight.
options.prompt: Sequence the chart: axes and title first, then the data, then the highlight, then the takeaway line; never show everything at once.
